newsitem.title: UK: Blair names left-winger Short to British cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Blair names left-winger Short to British cabinet.

text.p: New Prime Minister Tony Blair made further key appointments on Saturday to Britain's first Labour cabinet for 18 years, including outspoken left-winger Clare Short in his front-bench team.
Short, appointed minister for overseas development, told reporters she was "very pleased" with her new job.
She added:"I'm going to try to be good but I can't help it. I have to be me."

Political analysts had speculated that the moderate Blair, who won a landslide victory on Thursday after moving his party dramatically to the centre, might omit Short who has openly expressed misgivings about the direction of the party.

Among other key appointments, Marjorie "Mo" Mowlam was made Northern Ireland Secretary and was expected to fly straight to Belfast to tackle the thorny task of unblocking the peace process in the factionally riven British province.
Officials said she planned to go on a walkabout in the Northern Ireland capital, which on Thursday elected key Irish Republicans Gerry Adams and Martin McGuiness to seats in the London parliament.
Blair named a third woman, Harriet Harman, to be Social Security Secretary, reflecting Labour's desire to bring more women into the corridors of powers.
Ann Taylor was made leader of the House of Commons -- the ruling party's manager of parliamentary business who ensures smooth passage of legislation.
Blair has already named John Prescott his deputy prime minister and appointed his foreign, finance and education ministers.
He still has to complete the full line-up, which should be announced by Sunday.
